html:
Zhangzhung was an ancient kingdom of western Tibet, around the holy mountain of Kailash, from about 500 BCE until the Tibetan Empire conquered it in the 600s. Sources give the conquest as 625 or 644.

Early Tibetan texts remember the kings of Zhangzhung as the first rulers of the region. The Bon religion holds that its teachings came to Tibet through Zhangzhung, and a few Bon texts keep words of the lost Zhangzhung language. Archaeologists have found Iron Age forts and tombs in the area that fit a powerful state there.

The Yarlung king Songtsen Gampo first allied with Zhangzhung by marriage and then absorbed it into the Tibetan Empire. Its traditions lived on in Bon and, through it, in Tibetan Buddhism. It stands at the start of the history of Tibet as one land.
